title: Application of SEBAL Model for Inversing Catchment Evapotranspiration Based on MODIS Data
abstract: Surface evapotranspiration,as an important part of the land-atmospheric water cycle process,its reasonable and accurate estimation plays a significant role in understanding of water cycle and energy balance at the large scale catchment.First of all,the land cover in the upper reaches of the Hanjiang River Basin in 2001 is classified by adopting University of Maryland(UMD) classification mechanism and incorporating MODIS remote sensing data.And then the daily evapotranspiration is estimated by applying the SEBAL model-based surface energy balance algorithm.The results show that the average daily evapotranspiration of forest land has the largest value,and the grassland and the arable land follow.
keywords: Evapotranspiration; Environmental science; Water cycle; Water balance; Arable land; Drainage basin; Land cover; Energy balance; Hydrology (agriculture); Grassland; Remote sensing; Land use; Geography; Geology

title: Retrieving evapotranspiration of small watershed in loess hilly-gully region based on remote sensing image:taking Weigou Watershed as a case study
abstract: TM image and surface energy balance equation are used to estimate ET(evapotranspiration) of loess plateau Weigou Watershed.The estimation results are validated by lysimeter measured ET.And then,the correlation between ET and land use,surface parameters,terrain parameters is analyzed.Research shows that ET value ranges from 1.13 to 8.86 mm,with the average value of 4.94 mm on August 15,2003.Spatially,it increased from northwest to southeast.Different kinds of land have different ET value,the most is water and forest;the linear correlation between ET value and INDV is positive,and so are the degree of elevation;however,the linear correlation between ET value and surface temperature is negative.
keywords: Watershed; Evapotranspiration; Loess plateau; Lysimeter; Environmental science; Hydrology (agriculture); Terrain; Soil science; Remote sensing; Geology; Soil water; Geography; Cartography

title: Comparative analysis of regional evapotranspiration estimation models using remotely sensed data
abstract: Evapotranspiration plays a significant role in the earth's water and energy balance system. It affects regional and global climate, ecological environment and agricultural yield through the hydrological cycle. Remote sensing technique, which can provide representative regional surface parameters, has proven to be the only suitable approach to the estimation of large-area ET. This article summarizes and evaluates widely used models that were applied for predicting regional ET using satellite remotely sensed data and routine meteorological data, such as SEBAL and VITT. It is evident that quantitative ET retrieval with remotely sensed data at large scale has manifested its great prospect.
keywords: Regional evapotranspiration;Remote sensing;SEBAL;Single-layer model;Two-source model;VITT
venue: Nongye Gongcheng Xuebao Transactions of the Chinese Society of Agricultural Engineering

title: Remote Sensing Retrieval of Evapotranspiration over the Scale of Drainage Basin
abstract: Some primary land surface parameters needed in hydra-meteorology models can be retrieved from multispectra remote sensing data, and then the distribution map of Evapotranspiration(ET),which is very important in water resources management, can be made. Remote sensing retrieval of ET relates to some physical processes, and the validation and improvement of the retrieval results need to know about the techniques and methods to be used to monitor ET in situ, which is introduced briefly in this paper. Then the methods and development of retrieving ET by means of remote sensing are reviewed, especially the Surface Energy Balance Algorithm for Land(SEBAL in short) is demonstrated in detail.
keywords: Remote sensing; Evapotranspiration; Environmental science; Scale (ratio); Computer science; Geography; Cartography

title: Regional Analysis of Reference Crop Evapotranspiration Based on SPSS in Fushun
abstract: Based on the meteorological data collected from 3 stations in recent 10 years in Fushun region,the reference crop evapotranspiration(ET_0) was calculated with the Penman-Monteith equation recommended by FAO in 1990.The ET_0 of the region was analyzed using linear regression analysis based on software of SPSS.The results showed that the linear correlation was evident between the ET_0 data of Zhangdang and Xinbin stations,but it is not significant for the linear correlation between the Qingyuan and Xinbin station,neither between the Qingyuan and Zhangdang stations.The result will be helpful to analysis of the space distributions of the reference crop evapotranspiration in the region.
keywords: Evapotranspiration; Linear regression; Linear correlation; Regression analysis; Environmental science; Crop; Penman–Monteith equation; Hydrology (agriculture); Mathematics; Geography; Statistics; Forestry; Geology; Ecology

title: Decision Control System of Crop Water Requirement With Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The decision control support system is a system using Intel 8301 single chip microcomputer as main chip and Delta-T Devices Ltd etc Theta probe as soil environment sensor. The system realize data communication between single chip microcomputer and Pentium 4 computer serial port, which is developed by Visual Basic 6.0 programming language and C51 computer software, on the foundation of Penman formula. This decision control system is a system established by combining model and expert experience with artificial intelligent technology, as "Control system of water-saving agricultural Shanxi area". It can give decision control for scheme for the management of winter wheat and corn.
keywords: Irrigating Data Acquisition ADC decision serial communication
venue: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Test and Measurement

title: A study of evapotranspiration in Hailiutu river Basin, Ordos
abstract: Based on SEBS (Surface Energy Balance System), an inversion of evapotranspiration of dry season and rainy season in 2012 in Hailiutu river basin was carried out. The authors analyzed the spatial distribution of evapotranspiration, and discussed the effects caused by depth of groundwater level. The results show that, in dry season, the major factor of influence is the extent of moisture content of surface soil. In rainy season, the major factor of influence is the covered condition of vegetation and the extent of moisture content of surface soil. According to the result, the total evapotranspiration in Hailiutu river basin in 2012 is about 8. 76bou <sup>8</sup>m<sup>3</sup>.
keywords: Depth of groundwater level;Energy balance;Evapotranspiration;Hailiutu river basin

title: Using airborne Vis-NIR-TIR data and a surface energy balance model to map evapotranspiration at high spatial resolution
abstract: This paper presents the mapping.of surface energy fluxes in a Mediterranean agricultural region using two original tools. The first one is a set of high spatial resolution remote sensing data, allowing the consideration of 100 m size agricultural fields, and the second is a surface energy balance model that retrieves some variables of interest through the spatial variability depicted by the study area. The proposed approach was tested using field measurements on different crops during one year. The comparison showed that the key points of the model gave realistic results and that the energy flux estimates were in agreement with experimental reference measurements.
keywords: High spatial resolution;Single layer model;Spatial variability;Surface energy balance;Validation;VIS-NIR-TIR multidirectional remote sensing

title: Planning Management Method Based on MPCC in ETO Enterprise
abstract: There were many problems such as multi-project environment,variable task duration,project delay and man factors in planning management of ETO manufacturing enterprises.According to the multi-project critical chain(MPCC) theory,a new planning management process including planning template,planning scheduling and controlling were presented;every part was consisted of several steps;detailed application method of every step were designed.At last,multi-project environment that was three collateral products of one large power transformer enterprise was constructed and simulated by Crystal Ball software,the optimized product average cycle time was cut by 2.7 days.
keywords: Computer science; Project planning; Process management; Scheduling (production processes); Software; Operations management; Project management; Manufacturing engineering; Systems engineering; Operations research; Industrial engineering; Engineering; Operating system

title: Remote Sensing Analysis on Evapotranspiration Spatial Distribution Characteristics from Four-lake Wetland
abstract: Evapotranspiration spatial distribution from Four-lake wetland based on the MODIS and meteorology data was mapped by SEBAL model method in this paper.The similar results between the observed values from evaporation pan and calculated data from SEBAL model verified this method be suit for the studied wetland.The soil utilization was the main facor to cause the differences of evapotranspiration spatial distribution, in which the smallest evapotranspiration observed in city, then in dry land, paddy land, woodland, culture area and lake.The evapotranspiration was influenced mainly by the surface temperature and net radiation, and no NDVI impact was observed.
keywords: Evapotranspiration; Wetland; Environmental science; Woodland; Spatial distribution; Hydrology (agriculture); Pan evaporation; Normalized Difference Vegetation Index; Remote sensing; Geography; Geology; Ecology; Climate change

title: Estimating Evapotranspiration of Western Kentucky using SEBAL
abstract: Evapotranspiration is a vital aspect of the hydrological cycle, concerning 15% of the atmosphere's water vapor. Landsat ETM+, a USGS satellite, collects multispectal data of the Earth, with a return interval of 16 days. The Surface Energy Balance Algorithm for Land (SEBAL) is a model used to identify and quantify fluctuating hydrological energy. This project utilized cloud-free Landsat ETM+ data to calculate and quantify evapotranspiration of Western Kentucky in 1999 and 2002. The evapotranspiration values were then compared to land cover values to identify if land cover change has a significant effect on evapotranspiration.
keywords: Evapotranspiration; Environmental science; Remote sensing; Geography
venue: Murray State's Digital Commons (Murray State University)

title: 73. Verification of an NDVI-Evapotranspiration Model Using a Single Layer Model
abstract: To establish a method for estimating evapotranspiration from NDVI data, cloud free images were compiled by a new algorithm using a temporally varying function and land use data. The NDVI data set was used for the estimation of evapotranspiration, and the estimated flux was compared with the estimation of a single layer model. The comparison shows that the single layer model produces less evapotranspiration than the NDVI method based on water balance. The distribution patterns of evapotranspiration estimated by the two methods were quite similar, indicating that the NDVI method is effective in estimating evapotranspiration.
keywords: Evapotranspiration; Normalized Difference Vegetation Index; Data set; Environmental science; Water balance; Remote sensing; Mathematics; Geography; Statistics; Geology; Climate change

title: Research Advances on Land Surface Evapotranspiration Based on Remote Sensing Techonlogy
abstract: The development of the remote sensing technology provided a new method to estimate land surface evapotranspiration for the large areas.The theories of several methods of regional evapotranspiration,such as land surface energy balance and complementary relationship of land surface evapotranspiration were analyzed firstly.Based on the introduction of models and algorithms,the main merits and shortcomings about these models and algorithms were then discussed.Finally,the problems faced in the research of the land surface evapotranspiration based on the remote sensing technology and its future development trends were analyzed.
keywords: Evapotranspiration; Remote sensing; Geography; Environmental science; Energy balance; Surface (topology); Hydrology (agriculture); Geology; Mathematics; Ecology

title: Better predictability with "perfect" soil moisture
abstract: Potential predictability of surface air temperature and prediction over the United States for the National Centers for Environmental Prediction seasonal climate forecast GCM were conducted. Ensemble experiments were ran by forcing the GCM with observed sea surface temperatures (SSTs) from 1979 through 2000 and an estimate of observed soil moisture content. The latter was obtained by substituting the GCM simulated precipitation, which is used to drive the GCM's land-surface component, with observed pentad (five-day)-mean precipitation at each time step of the model's integration. The resultant data were analyzed in detail.
venue: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society

title: Evapotranspiration modules for crop growth simulation. Implementation of the algorithms from Penman, Makkink and Priestley-Taylor
abstract: Calculation of evapotranspiration is essential for the estimation of crop water use or for studying the effect of drought stress on crop performance with simulation models. Several methods are available for calculation of evapotranspiration. This report describes three different methods : the Penman method (1948) and the approaches of Makkink (1957) and Priestley -Taylor (1972). The modules described in this report are developed for use in general crop growth models for water-limited conditions, such as in Van Laar et al. (1992). The application of the modules, however, is not limited to the SUCROS type models.
keywords: Evapotranspiration; Crop; Agricultural engineering; Mathematics; Algorithm; Computer science; Hydrology (agriculture); Geography; Forestry; Engineering; Ecology; Geotechnical engineering

title: Metrics and process description for CAD-Platform automation of ETO products - Literature Review.
abstract: The performance of Organizations that create Engineered to order (ETO) discrete products with the help of 3DCAD tools and Product Lines Engineering (PLE) approach require a set of metrics in order to evaluate its capability to create 3DCAD platforms. This paper researches literature and software documentation for describing-and-measuring the processes that conform that connection between PLE and CAD for ETO products. The references are classified according intersections of research fields, and a summary with keywords added. No relevant literature was found so the need for research on this subject is presented.
keywords: ETO;Metrics;PLE;Product family;Product Platform

title: Interactive computer system for estimating monthly evapotranspiration
abstract: An integrated software package has been developed for estimating monthly evapotranspiration (ET), effective precipitation, and crop irrigation requirements in the western United States. A user can identify weather data available in a region of interest, compare the performance of ET estimation methods at various sites, create and edit input data sets, perform Blaney-Criddle ET computations, and view graphical results. All of this is done in an interactive graphics environment under menu control. The system overcomes many of the difficulties traditionally encountered in the process of making ET estimates.

title: PENGARUH PROMOSI JABATAN, KOMPETENSI, DAN ETOS KERJA ISLAM TERHADAP KINERJA KARYAWAN(Studi Kasus Pada BPRS Bangun Drajat Warga Yogyakarta)
abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of job promotion, competene, and Islamic work ethic on employee performance at BPRS Bangun Drajat Warga Yogyakarta. The method of analysis used multiple regression analysis using SPSS 23.0 software. The sampling technique used is purposive sampling. Primary data in this study were obtained from respondents. The number of population in this study were 34 respondents. The results of this study indicate that job promotion and Islamic work ethic have no effect on employee performance, while competence has a positive and significant effect eon employee performance.
keywords: Nonprobability sampling; Work ethic; Promotion (chess); Business administration; Competence (human resources); Psychology; Islam; Population; Work (physics); Social psychology; Political science; Business; Sociology; Theology; Engineering; Demography

title: Annual evapotranspiration in oases of the Tarim basin based on a coupled water-energy balance
abstract: A coupled water-energy balance model was developed to analyze the water resources use in arid oases. The sum of the annual irrigation and precipitation was taken as the water availability for the oasis. The Budyko hypothesis was extended by using the Fu Baopu's equation. The model was verified by data for precipitation, irrigation, runoff and potential evapotranspiration for 5 large oases in the Tarim basin in China from 1971 to 2004. An empirical relationship for estimating the model parameters is presented based on the annual evapotranspiration and land use in the Akesu oasis in the Tarim basin.
keywords: Budyko hypothesis;Coupled water-energy balance;Evapotranspiration;Oases in Tarim basin
venue: Qinghua Daxue Xuebao Journal of Tsinghua University

title: Crop water requirement and irrigation water requirement of mustard crop at selected locations of Chhattisgarh State, India
abstract: The present study aimed to find out the crop water and irrigation water requirement for mustard crop over three locations of Chhattisgarh state to represent three agro climatic zones. Results revealed that highest crop water requirement (373 mm) and irrigation requirement (333 mm) is noticed at Raipur which is representing the Chhattisgarh Plain zone and lowest at Ambikapur (328 mm and 283 mm) of Northern Hill zone. Stage-wise information of irrigation water requirement for mustard crop would help judicious utilisation of available water and may reduce the over utilisation of ground water source.
keywords: Crop water requirement;CROPWAT;Effective rainfall;Irrigation water requirement

title: Study on Regional Evapotranspiration Model Based onRemote Sensing Method
abstract: It is a new method to estimate land surface evapotranspiration of large region by using remote sensing. This paper analyzes several remote sensing models of land surface evapotranspiration such as Land Surface Energy Balance, Complementary Relationship of Land Surface Evapotranspiration, Penman Montieth and Climatology Method of Regional Evapotranspiration. Methods to derive land surface parameters from remote sensing data are given. The paper meteres include Albedo, NDVI, Surface temperature and Emissivity, which are used widely at home and abroad. The relationship among them are delineated.
keywords: Evapotranspiration; Albedo (alchemy); Environmental science; Remote sensing; Emissivity; Energy balance; Geography

title: Richard's equation approach to the design of evapotranspiration beds
abstract: Evapotranspiration (ET) bed design commonly uses a simple mass balance (SMB) approach to determine adequate depth and area for on-site wastewater treatment systems. The SMB approaches tend to oversimplify interactions among water, soil, and plants. This article proposes an alternative approach to ET bed design that utilizes the Richards equation simulation model and a well-known groundwater modeling computer program. Results indicate that this approach more accurately represents an actual system because it includes consideration of the dynamics of the soil-water-plant system. -from Authors
venue: Transactions American Society of Agricultural Engineers

title: RETRIEVAL OF EVAPOTRANSPIRATION IN CONTIGUOUS AREA OF HEBEI-INNER MONGOLIA BASED ON SEBAL MODEL
abstract: Contiguous area in Hebei-Inner Mongolia was selected for this study.SEBAL model combined with Landsat TM5 image and meteorological data from 10 stations near the contiguous area were used to induce daily LUCC evapotranspiration.Compared with evapotranspiration data from Zhangjiakou water bureau,the accuracy of induction was high.These data revealed that evapotranspiration of water and woodland showed double peaks.Daily evapotranspiration was in descending order: woodland,water,grassland,residential point,unutilized land,cultivated land,sandy land.
keywords: Evapotranspiration; Woodland; Grassland; Environmental science; Inner mongolia; Hydrology (agriculture); Land use; Geography; Geology; Ecology; China

title: Design and Realization of A Hardware Firewall Based on ETOS
abstract: The embedded operating system ETOS self-developed by Qingdao Yeetec Technology Co., Ltd. is introduced. After analyzed firewall platform Firewall-R1, the realization of a hardware firewall based on ETOS is introduced in details. Then the implementation of the firewall in the ETOS kernel is analyzed, and particularly to explain the software realization of the hardware firewall. The firewall has been used in the network products of Qingdao Yeetec Technology Co., Ltd. Experimental results indicate the firewall is stable, safe and high efficient.
keywords: Firewall (physics); Application firewall; Computer science; Context-based access control; Operating system; Embedded system; Stateful firewall; Computer hardware; Computer security; Business

title: A Decision Support System for Prediction of Crop Yield, Evapotranspiration, and Irrigation Management
abstract: Computer simulation models have been developed which predict growth, development, and yield for grain legumes. These models can be applied for yield prediction as well as water management decisions. The soybean and peanut models, SOYGRO and PNUTGRO, were used to generate longterm yield, evapotranspiration, and irrigation demand for Gainesville, FL, and Tifton, GA, for six different soils. High yield levels were a function of location and total irrigation, while low yields were a function of location and soil water holding characteristics.
keywords: Evapotranspiration; Irrigation; Yield (engineering); Tifton; Deficit irrigation; Soil water; Irrigation management; Environmental science; Agricultural engineering; Agronomy; Mathematics; Hydrology (agriculture); Soil science; Engineering; Forage

title: Software and data for Journal Article "Complementary relationship-derived actual evapotranspiration for operational drought monitoring"
abstract: Included in this archive are the datasets and software utilized to produce a gridded actual evapotranspiration (ETa) product, following the complementary relationship (CR) methodology detailed in "Complementary Relationship-derived Actual Evapotranspiration for Operational Drought Monitoring" (Journal of Hydrometeorology, 2026). The software provided was employed to calculate ETa values and CR fitting parameters. Furthermore, the data files encompass both the final ETa grid products and the intermediate data required for their generation.
keywords: Evapotranspiration; Software; Grid; Computer software; Data processing
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Decision support system for prediction of crop yield, evapotranspiration, and irrigation management
abstract: Computer simulation models have been developed which predict growth, development, and yield for grain legumes. These models can be applied for yield prediction as well as water management decisions. The soybean and peanut models, SOYGRO and PNUTGRO, were used to generate longterm yield, evapotranspiration, and irrigation demand for Gainesville, FL, and Tifton, GA, for six different soils. High yield levels were a function of location and total irrigation, while low yields were a function of location and soil water holding characteristics.

title: The comparison of modelled and measured evapotranspiration for different land use units
abstract: The modelling system THESEUS (= Toolbox for Hydro-Ecological Simulation and Evaluation Utilities) from Wegehenkel (1997 a, 1998) was used in this study. Using this model, it is possible to estimate the evapotranspiration of a chosen agricultural field (or landscape) with one day time step. The value of evapotranspiration obtained by the model were compared with measurements of evapotranspiration by the use of modified Bowen ratio method. The comparison of modelled and measured values of evapotranspiration show a very good agreement.
keywords: Evapotranspiration;Modelling;Water balance

title: Two-layer parametrization of evapotranspiration for use in a mesometeorological model
abstract: A two-layer model of the vegetation cover based on Deardorff's approach is described. The sensitivity of the model to variations of the parameters characterizing the state of the soil, vegetation, and atmosphere is evaluated. Verification of the model is carried out on the basis of observation data in accordance with the KUREX-88 program on four types of farmlands. A comparison of the measured and calculated values of the components of the heat balance and of the characteristics of stomatal resistance gave satisfactory results.

title: Ensemble monthly evapotranspiration over italy 1991-2020
abstract: Six open access actual ET datasets are merged using an expert-based multiple collocation (MC) approach, with the aim of reconstructing a spatiotemporal consistent monthly dataset for the climatological period 1991-2020 over Italy at a spatial resolution of 1-km. The merged products include: three water balance datasets (BIG BANG, LSA SAF, and LISFLOOD), two residual surface energy balance models (SSEBop, and ALEXI) and the MODIS standard product. More details can be found in Cammalleri et al. (2023, under review)

title: Vergleich modellierter und gemessener Evapotranspiration für verschiedene Fruchtarten in Nord-Mitteleuropa
abstract: Mit Hilfe des Modellierungssystems THESEUS (Toolbox for HydroEcological Simulation and Evaluation Utilities) von WEGEHENKEL [We05] ist es moglich, die Evapotranspiration einer landwirtschaftlichen Nutzflache oder eines Biotops in definierten Zeitabschnitten zu bestimmen. Die vom Modell berechneten Werte der Evapotranspiration wurden verglichen mit Messungen, die auf der modifizierten Bowen-Verhaltnis-Methode beruhen. Die vom Modell berechneten Werte zeigen eine sehr gute Ubereinstimmung mit den gemessenen Werten.

title: Online Remote-Sensing Tool for Calculating Evapotranspiration

title: Standard reference evapotranspiration calculations: REF-ET
abstract: REF-ET is a PC software program for computing standard calculations of reference evapotranspiration (E<inf>to</inf>) and associated variables. Computations are based on recommendations presented in ASCE Manual 70. The REF-ET software is intended to supplement E<inf>to</inf> computation routines written and used by professionals, consultants and others by serving as a computation and comparison check for these production routines.
